scripts.title: The $11,500 Word doc
scripts.note: Story, then the fix. Phone in hand for the hook, eyes on the lens from 'Look… this isn't about the wiring.' The blurred bid crops cut in over 0:06 to 0:27 in the edit, and the same-day proposal demo over 0:34 to 0:48. Never name or show the contractor.
scripts.source: Sammy's own electrical bid (Word .docx in Google Drive, dated Sept 23, 2026): Base Bid $11,500.00; the scope lists 296 devices (60+95+1+5+7+8+40+40+4+23+3+4+1+5); exclusions include 'Scopes not mentioned on GC bid form'; printed X signature line; 100% upon completion. 'Nearly five days' after the walk and the $12,000+ generic Word invoice are Sammy's account (invoice not on file yet).
scripts.script:
An electrician walked my house.
Five days later… he sent me a Word doc.
Eleven thousand five hundred dollars.

No link. No options. No photos.
Two hundred ninety-six outlets, switches and lights… one number.
The fine print says scopes not mentioned on the GC bid form.
There's no GC. It's my house.

To say yes, I had to print it, sign the X and send it back.
Then the invoice came. A generic Word template.
Twelve grand and change.

Look… this isn't about the wiring.
It's about the five days.
Five days is plenty of time for a homeowner to call the next guy.

Here's the fix.
You finish the walk… and before you leave the driveway, they have a link.
Your logo. Photos from the walk. Three options.
They sign on their phone and pay the deposit.
Job's done? The invoice sends itself with a pay button… and asks for the review.

If your proposals still live in Word… DM me PROPOSAL.
I'll show you what yours looks like rebuilt.
scripts.caption:
An electrician walked my house. Five days later he sent me a Word doc for $11,500. Then a generic Word invoice for $12K+.

This isn't about the wiring. It's about the five days. That's plenty of time for a homeowner to call the next guy.

The fix: a proposal link before you leave the driveway. Your logo, photos from the walk, three options. They sign and pay the deposit from their phone. When the job's done, the invoice sends itself with a pay button and asks for the review.
